newsitem.title: UK: Saudi American Bank plans first Saudi fund on LSE.
newsitem.headline: Saudi American Bank plans first Saudi fund on LSE.

text.p: Saudi American Bank (SAMBA) said on Monday it planned to launch an investment company that will, for the first time, allow international investors access to Saudi Arabian equities.
SAMBA said the Saudi Arabia Investment Fund Ltd (SAIF) will be a closed ended fund and is seeking a listing on the London Stock Exchange towards the end of July.

The bank said the fund will have a market capitalisation of about $200 million and its investment objective was to achieve long-term capital appreciation through a diversified portfolio, mainly of equities listed on the Saudi stock market.
SAIF is being sponsored by Baring Brothers Ltd and is being marketed to institutions in Europe, the U.S., the Far East and Middle East.
SAMBA said 70 stocks were listed on the Saudi stock market, which had a market capitalisation of around $48.7 billion on April 30, 1997.
The bank said it expected the Saudi stock market to expand as a source for private equity capital, using its up to date clearance and settlement system.
